incidents.cause: Operation of the airplane by a non-certificated pilot. Contributing to the accident was the non-certificated pilot’s failure to maintain airspeed while making a forced landing following a total loss of engine power at low altitude, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall. Also contributing was the pi
The pilot’s improper fuel management, which resulted in fuel exhaustion and a total loss of engine power.

Airspeed was not maintained, which resulted in a loss of control and the airplane entering into a stall/spin to the ground. Contributing to the accident was a loss of engine power due to carburetor icing.
A total loss of engine power for undetermined reasons.
The pilot's inadequate fuel management, which resulted in a loss of engine power due to fuel starvation.
The pilot's inadequate visual lookout and failure to maintain clearance from a tree.
The pilot's improper descent below the published minimum descent altitude during the approach, which resulted in controlled flight into terrain.

The student pilot's failure to execute a go-around in timely manner, which resulted in a collision with terrain.  Also causal was the instructor's inadequate supervision of the flight and delayed remedial actions.
Total loss of engine power during the landing approach due to insect debris in the carburetor metering valve, which resulted in fuel starvation.
The pilot's failure to maintain a proper glide path while on final approach.

The pilot's improper pre-flight planning and failure to ensure that there was an adequate fuel supply on board to complete the flight, which resulted in fuel exhaustion. Contributing to the accident was the malfunction of the fuel quantity indicator.
The loss of engine power for undetermined reasons.
The pilot's failure to properly secure the airplane before a hand propeller start, which resulted in the airplane moving forward and colliding with maintenance equipment.
The pilot's excessive use of brakes during a rejected takeoff, resulting in a nose over.
The loss of pitch control due to slippage of the elevator control cable resulting from the maintenance personnel’s improper installation and inspection of the cable.
The pilot's unstabilized approach, which resulted in landing long and fast, and his subsequent failure to maintain clearance from trees during a go-around.
A loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion. A factor in the accident was the pilot's inadequate preflight inspection.
The pilot's improper fuel management, which led to fuel exhaustion and a subsequent forced landing on a road too narrow for the airplane.
The pilot’s failure to maintain control of the airplane after landing on a grass taxiway with a tailwind, which resulted in a nose over.
Failure of the left main landing gear strut during the landing roll due to a preexisting crack.

The flight instructor’s inadequate supervision of the flight and improper decision to continue with a takeoff after the airplane swerved off the runway. Contributing to the accident was the student pilot’s failure to maintain directional control of the tailwheel-equipped airplane.
A loss of engine power for reasons that could not be determined because the aircraft sank after ditching and was not recovered.
The pilot's inadequate compensation for wind conditions.
A loss of engine power during takeoff/initial climb for an undetermined reason.
The pilot's exceedance of the critical angle of attack while maneuvering at low altitude, which resulted in an accelerated aerodynamic stall, spin, and impact with terrain.

An inadequate 100-hour maintenance inspection that failed to detect and correct loose nuts on a single-drive dual magneto, which led to the subsequent separation of the magneto from the engine during initial climb and the total loss of engine power.
The collapse of the right main landing gear during the turn off the runway due to the failure of the A-frame assembly.

The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during a simulated left engine failure during takeoff. Also causal to the accident was the flight instructor's delayed remedial action to maintain directional control and reduce the right engine mixture control.
The pilot's improper fuel planning, which resulted in fuel exhaustion and  a total loss of power to both engines.
The pilot’s failure to maintain aircraft control during landing.  Contributing to the accident were the crosswind wind conditions and terrain induced turbulence.
The pilot’s failure to maintain directional control during the landing and attempted go-around.

The pilot’s failure to maintain airplane control and the resulting encounter with an aerodynamic stall. Also causal were the pilot’s inadequate preflight planning and preflight inspection, his failure to ensure the pitch trim was positioned correctly for takeoff, his decision to operate the airplane
The fatigue failure of the left main landing gear enhanced side brace assembly.

The pilot receiving instruction's failure to maintain a proper approach path and her delayed go-around during a simulated emergency landing, which resulted in landing short of the runway. Contributing to the accident was the flight instructor's failure to properly monitor the student's approach.
The flight instructor's delayed remedial action during a simulated engine failure on takeoff, which resulted in a loss of directional control.

The pilot's failure to maintain sufficient altitude above mountainous terrain while maneuvering during night conditions in an area prone to turbulence, which resulted in a collision with terrain. Contributing to the accident was the flight instructor's decision to conduct maneuvers over mountainous

The student pilot's inadequate compensation for the gusting crosswind conditions and the certified flight instructor's inadequate supervision, resulting in a loss of directional control during landing.
The instructor's failure to obtain the proper touchdown point in a multiengine airplane, during a single-engine approach in a strong gusty headwind.
The pilot's inadvertent encounter with an unexpected intense rain shower with severe turbulence at night.
The pilot's failure to properly manage fuel which resulted in fuel exhaustion and subsequent loss of power to the forward engine.

The air traffic controller’s failure to properly scan the runway and local area, and their general loss of situational awareness, resulting in a near midair collision. Contributing to the incident was the Cessna 337 pilot's poor decision making when he failed to fly the standard downwind leg distanc
The failure of a bearing in the fuel control unit, which resulted in fuel starvation and a total loss of engine power.
The pilot’s improper decision to continue flight in deteriorating weather conditions, which resulted in collision with the ground.
The pilot's failure to maintain lateral/bank control during the initial climb in turbulent conditions.
The pilot's failure to ensure that the tailwheel pin was in the locked position prior to the takeoff roll, resulting in a runway excursion, ground loop, and substantial damage.

The pilot's inadequate preflight fuel planning, his reliance on the fuel flow indicator without verifying the initial fuel level input, and his improper decision to continue the flight with the low fuel light illuminated, which resulted in fuel exhaustion, the subsequent total loss of engine power,
The pilot’s abrupt maneuver to avoid hay bales during the takeoff roll, which resulted in a loss of directional control.
The pilot’s failure to maintain lateral control while maneuvering at a low altitude.
The pilot’s failure to see and avoid a pole during an agricultural application flight.
The pilot's decision to take off with a gusting tailwind and his subsequent failure to maintain directional control.
The pilot’s failure to maintain clearance from mountainous terrain.
The student pilot’s failure to maintain directional control during the landing flare.
The pilot’s improper landing flare and subsequent failure to maintain directional control during landing.
The student pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll.

The student pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed while maneuvering, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall and spin. Contributing to the accident was the student pilot's failure to properly assess her physical condition prior to conducting the flight.
The glider’s encounter with atmospheric conditions where the lift was not sufficient to maintain flight, which resulted in the pilot landing short of the intended runway.

The failure of the flight instructor  to move his glider from an active runway in accordance with procedures due to his distraction by having a conversation with the air boss, which resulted in the landing glider colliding with the glider on the runway.

The failure of the other flight instructor to move his glider from the active runway in accordance with procedures due to his distraction by having a conversation with the air boss, which resulted in the landing glider colliding with the glider on the runway.

The pilot's encounter with atmospheric conditions that resulted in a loss of lift and a subsequent loss of control near terrain that precluded recovery. The pilot's failure to maintain glider control and his exceedance of the glider's critical angle of attack while maneuvering in gusting wind conditions, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall.
Collision with a bird in flight, which resulted in damage to the engine, a fuel leak, and a subsequent total loss of engine power due to fuel exhaustion.
The student pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a bounced landing, and his subsequent loss of directional control and a hard landing.
The student pilot’s improper recovery from a power-off stall. Contributing to the accident was the flight instructor’s failure to properly monitor the student pilot during the stall recovery.
